scope: Six siege machine sheets only; Ottoman distinct cannon remains existing v6.
frameContract: [sourceX,sourceY,width,height,groundAnchorXRelative,groundAnchorYRelative]. Read measured rectangles; generated rows do not line up with exact image quarter boundaries.
scaleContract: Use stable bodyHeight/rowBodyHeights across all states. Arm/sling extensions increase crop extent, not actor scale. Machine nominal target heights and visible crew calibration are both supplied for integration choice.
groundAnchorMethod: Approximate chassis contact center: horizontal midpoint of authored group and measured source ground-plane inset above lowest foot/wheel pixel. Sprite owner can refine anchors visually without editing source.

historicalBoundaries.roman: Late Roman engineering; torsion single arm with flexible sling, no counterweight. Covered ram protection is artistic interpretation.
historicalBoundaries.persian: Sasanian inspiration (224–651 CE); covered oxhide ram supported by Ammianus20.7; stone engine mechanism is an artistic inference, not a claimed exact reconstruction. No Achaemenid counterweight.
historicalBoundaries.tang: Human traction beam and rope pulls, no counterweight/gunpowder. Taibai Yinjing bookIV chapter35.
historicalBoundaries.mongol: 13th-century adoption of western specialist counterweight engineering, associated with Xiangyang1272–73; not a native Mongol invention.

sources.locator: Li Quan, Taibai Yinjing, bookIV, 攻城具篇35

Subject: late-Roman covered battering ram, the Roman testudo-style shelter. A LONG LOW rectangular timber wheeled chassis, four modest spoked wheels, sturdy cross-braced posts, pitched protective hide roof with dull red leather/hide strips over planks, a long horizontal suspended battering beam on chains below the roof with an iron ram-head at the leading end. This is a Roman covered ram, NOT a catapult, no throwing arm, no counterweight. Shape elongated and low, horizontal log prominent, roof squared consistent. Rows1–2 ram beam in neutral pushing position; row3 horizontal log visibly drawn BACK into shelter by crew; row4 same log swung/pushed FORWARD with ram-head projecting beyond roof.
